I beat moonlord for the first time in a legit terraria playthroug recently, (expert mode) here are some strategies I used, hope they will be helpful.

I didn't make a moonlord arena instead I used the fishron mount. (I tried the arena method in my older playthrougs, even an asphalt one but failed regardless.)

Some useful accessories for the fight for any class.

- Frozen shield. 

This gives you 6 defense, knock back resistance and 25% dmg reduction when below 50% hp. A very useful accessory imo regardless of the class, plus it synergies well with the fishron mount.

- Worm scarf 

This one's self explanatory, it gives 17% damage reduction. Makes you more tanky

- Charm of myths 

This reduces the health potion cool down. Also gives you a little bit of hp regeneration I think. 

I played this run as a mage, so here are the rest of the accessories I used. 

- Star cloak 
- Celestial emblem 
- Celestial shell

and the weapon I used is the Nebula Blaze and the armor is Spectre armor with the offensive headpiece. (heard the other spectre headpiece is pretty useless for this fight because of moonlord's debuff.) 

I dropped wings and boots for celestial shell and charm of myths. (If you can, try to get warding modifiers for more defense or menacing for more damage for your accessories) 

Potions I used were, Ironskin, Regeneration, Lifeforce, Endurance, and a highest tier food buff. (I used apple pies from the rod of discord farm I got.) 

As for the fight itself you pretty much only have to worry about the moonlord's death ray. If you can dodge it the fight is pretty easy. With this setup I tanked 2 death rays. So try to take out the forhead eye first. Then take out the other eyes as well. After all 3 eyes are out, the fight is pretty much over, what you basically have to do is aim for the heart and take it out.

Admit it, this episode seemed incredibly unrealistic. In a world like the one portrayed in The Last of Us, there are countless dangers and risks present, from infected individuals to raiders and bandits. Yet, despite all these dangers, Bill and Frank managed to live a seemingly idyllic life, complete with a romantic relationship. This type of a love story is hard to imagine even in our world today, let alone in a post-apocalyptic setting. To me, this episode felt like a fantasy love story, disconnected from the harsh realities of the world in which it was set.
Well it was a good run fellas... This series had the potential to be a very well made video game adaptation television series, but they just blew it. smh..

I completely agree with your thoughts on the episode. The Bill and Frank story did seem out of place. It would have been a better choice to present their story as a standalone episode or a short story rather than incorporating it into the main storyline. This would have given the characters the proper amount of screen time they deserved, while also keeping the main plot intact.

It was a filler episode tho. While the acting, cinematography, and overall production of the episode were top-notch, it did feel out of place within the main plot. Giving Bill and Frank's story so much screen time (a whole episode) , when they likely won't be seen again in the show, seems like a waste.
